items.title: Linux Lands Fix for Rare, Varying SMP Boot Hangs Affecting Kernels Since 2024
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Among the flurry of last minute patch activity ahead of tomorrow's presumed Linux 7.3 stable kernel release is a fix for addressing some rare hangs at boot time. The reports varied but ultimately tracked down to a kernel change made two years ago...</article>

items.title: GNOME's New Local/Cloud AI Chat App Gains More Features
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Coming about the past few months has been Moose as a GNOME-aligned AI chat application built around GTK4 and libadwaita. It began as a local AI chat app for the GNOME desktop and grew to support cloud AI services as well. This past week marked the latest feature release for Moose...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Lands Last-Minute Fixes For Samsung 990 PRO & 990 EVO Plus SSDs
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Ahead of the Linux 7.3 stable kernel expected to be released tomorrow, last minute workarounds were merged for the Samsung 990 PRO and Samsung 990 EVO Plus NVMe solid state drives...</article>

items.title: KDE Plasma 6.9 To Debut New Weather Widget & On-Screen Keyboard
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With KDE Plasma 6.8 released earlier this week, KDE developers have begun working on more feature activity toward Plasma 6.9...</article>

items.title: Ubuntu Touch 24.04-2.1 Brings New Hardware Support & Important Security Fix
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Ubuntu Touch 24.04-2.1 was released on Friday as the latest update to this community-maintained tablet/smartphone Ubuntu Linux platform. Ubuntu Touch 24.04-1.5 was also released as a maintenance update for the prior series...</article>

items.title: Wine 11.20 Released With CD-ROM Support Change
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Wine 11.20 is out today as the newest bi-weekly development release of this software for enjoying Windows games and apps on Linux. We are quickly approaching the point where this development work will culminate into the Wine 12.0 stable release in early 2027...</article>

items.title: 17 More Security Vulnerabilities Made Public For X.Org Libraries
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Just shy of two weeks since a dozen vulnerabilities were published for the X.Org Server and XWayland, more than one dozen vulnerabilities were made public today affecting multiple X.Org client libraries...</article>

items.title: GNOME OS Preview Announced In Road Toward A Stable Release
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The GNOME OS Linux distribution to date has just been in GNOME OS Nightly form for tracking the latest nightly packages of GNOME in their current development form. GNOME OS Preview was announced today as their trek toward a stable GNOME OS in using the latest GNOME stable releases rather than nightly form...</article>

items.title: The Best Features Of Linux 7.3: Performance Improvements, Lots From Valve
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The Linux 7.3 kernel is slated to be officially released on Sunday, 18 October, barring any last minute issues from coming about. With that said, here's a reminder about some of the most exciting features to look forward to in this next kernel version...</article>

items.title: After 23 Years, Longtime Linux Developer To "Step Back For A While"
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Longtime Linux kernel engineer Darrick Wong who stepped down as the XFS file-system maintainer in 2023 is now taking a step back from his other Linux kernel development roles after working on the kernel the past 23 years...</article>

items.title: Intel Xeon 6980P Granite Rapids Performance On Linux Over The Past Year
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>It's been nearly one year since receiving the Gigabyte R284-A92-AAL1 2U Granite Rapids server platform for continuing my testing of the flagship Xeon 6980P processors. Curious how the Xeon 6980P 2P performance has evolved on Linux since then, I ran some benchmarks on the newly-released Ubuntu Server 26.10 against the tests carried out last year on Ubuntu 25.10 with the same hardware.</article>

items.title: AI-Generated Starling Desktop Environment Rolls Out Its Own Office Suite
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Starling, the open-source desktop environment written in Swift and with its own Wayland compositor too and written largely via Claude Code, has now rolled out its own AI-generated office suite...</article>

items.title: Fedora 46 Looking At Moving To RPM v6 Package Format
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The RPM v4 packaging format has been used by Red Hat Enterprise Linux and Fedora and its derivatives for more than two decades. With next year's Fedora 46 release, Fedora Linux may finally transition to the modern RPM v6 packaging format...</article>

items.title: AI Resurrects AVX-512 Support For Mesa's LLVMpipe Software Driver
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With pending code for Mesa, the LLVMpipe software-based Gallium3D/OpenGL driver could soon become faster on modern systems that support AVX-512. That's assuming the AI/LLVM-generated code is all in order...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.4 To Enable Intel Instruction Timeout For Fending Off TDX VM DoS Attacks
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Linux 7.4 is enabling support for a new Intel CPU feature for providing safety against possible denial of service attacks using Trust Domain Extensions "TDX" VMs. The new feature is Intel Instruction Timeout and previously in-development known as Notify VM Exit...</article>

items.title: Linux 7.3 Squeezes Even More Performance Out Of The AMD Threadripper PRO 9995WX
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the Linux 7.3 kernel due out for release on Sunday, I've continued running more benchmarks recently of this forthcoming kernel version and it looks great. In my Linux 7.3 testing of the Git state it's been looking great in testing on a variety of hardware shown across multiple systems. Recently I decided to try out this new kernel code on the 96-core AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 9995WX workstation...</article>

items.title: Intel LLM-Scaler-vLLM PV 1.5 Brings Big Improvements
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Intel software engineers today released the latest version of LLM-Scaler-vLLM PV 1.5, their containerized Docker stack providing a convenient AI/LLM experience atop Intel Arc Graphics hardware and born out of their Project Battlematrix initiative...</article>

items.title: Mesa's Zink Now Offers VA-API Video Acceleration Atop Vulkan Video
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Merged today to Mesa is initial video acceleration support for the generic Zink Gallium3D driver built atop the Vulkan APIs. What this implementation allows is exposing Video Acceleration API (VA-API) implemented atop the Vulkan Video interfaces...</article>

items.title: Fedora 45 Will Not Be Released Next Week
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those eager to run the pristine Fedora 45 media, you will need to wait at least one more week...</article>

items.title: Today's Steam Beta Makes The Linux Client A 64-bit App
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Valve just dropped a new Steam client beta and it's a big one for Linux gamers...</article>

items.title: Intel Nova Lake S & Nova Lake P To Support SR-IOV With Xe Graphics
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>A patch has been posted to the Linux kernel mailing list by an Intel engineer confirming that Nova Lake S and Nova Lake P processors with integrated graphics will support SR-IOV in conjunction with the Xe kernel graphics driver...</article>

items.title: LPDDR5 5467 vs. 6400 vs. 7467 MT/s Memory Performance Benchmarks For Laptops
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>With the recently reviewed Star Labs StarFighter Ultra Linux laptop its BIOS allows for configurable memory speeds unlike many other laptop vendor BIOS implementations these days. Star Labs also made the default design decision to run the LPDDR5-7467 rated memory at LPDDR5-6400 speeds in the name of a balanced user experience for power/performance. So I was curious to run some benchmarks quantifying that power and performance impact of LPDDR5-6400 vs. LPDDR5-7467 plus tossed in LPDDR5-5467 testing as well as the third choice offered with this StarFighter Ultra laptop.</article>

items.title: Memtest86+ v9.00 Released With Support For ARM64 Memory Testing
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>The open-source Memtest86+ program that is popular for RAM testing has expanded beyond the x86/x86_64 (and LoongArch64) world to now support memory testing on ARM64/AArch64 hardware...</article>

items.title: 3mdeb Releases Updated Dasharo/Coreboot Firmware For ASRock Rack SPC741D8-2L2T
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>3mdeb firmware engineers have been quite busy this year working on porting Coreboot and openSIL to an AMD Ryzen AM5 MSI motherboard and similarly getting openSIL and Coreboot up and running on a Gigabyte server motherboard for AMD EPYC 9005 CPUs. They haven't forgotten about their past projects though and today released an updated version of their Dasharo downstream firmware for the ASRock Rack SPC741D8-2L2T motherboard supporting 4th and 5th Gen Xeon Scalable processors...</article>

items.title: Claude Code / AI Shows Potential For Reverse-Engineering Hardware For Linux Support
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>AI/LLMs like Claude Code are beginning to prove capable of helping to reverse engineer hardware for Linux support, especially when it comes to the tedious reverse engineering tasks...</article>

items.title: Ubuntu 26.10 Released With Linux 7.3 + GNOME 51, Rust Coreutils Migration Complete
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Ubuntu 26.10 "Stonking Stingray" is now officially available as the newest six-month non-LTS update to Ubuntu Linux...</article>

items.title: Huawei Proposes Enabling CPU Boost By Default For ACPI CPPC Linux Driver
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>For those using the generic ACPI Collaborative Processor Performance Control (CPPC) CPUFreq driver such as on a number of ARM64 Linux server platforms, if the CPUs support a "boost" mode it's disabled by default. But a patch from Huawei is now looking to enable CPU boost mode by default on Linux...</article>

items.title: GNOME Mutter Improves Damage Tracking For Secondary GPU Copy Buffers
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>As an early improvement to Mutter to look forward to with GNOME 52 (Update: It will first appear in GNOME 51.2), the compositor is now tracking damage for secondary GPU copy buffers. This should improve the experience for those with multi-GPU setups such as some hybrid laptops...</article>

items.title: Microsoft Releases Microsoft Defender For The Linux Desktop
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Microsoft's newest software release for Linux is... Microsoft Defender for the Linux desktop. Microsoft Defender has been ported to Linux to "secure Linux desktops" with Microsoft acknowledging that "more developers begin to use Linux desktops" and thus bringing their security application and threat-protection product to Linux desktops to complement their prior ill-used Linux server support...</article>

items.title: Framework Computers Triples Their Financial Support To CachyOS
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In addition to providing Framework systems to the CachyOS Linux distribution for optimizing the support, Framework Computers has also been providing monthly donations to the project. CachyOS confirmed today that Framework Computers has now tripled their monthly donations to this independent Linux distribution built atop Arch Linux...</article>

items.title: Apple Contributes SSAF Driver To LLVM Clang For Source Code Transformations
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>Apple compiler engineers have contributed to upstream LLVM/Clang today a Scalable Static Analysis Framework (SSAF) driver for whole-program based analysis and source-to-source code transformations...</article>

items.title: Epic Games To Improve Easy Anti-Cheat On Linux With Anti-Cheat Systemd Service & eBPF
items.author: Michael Larabel
items.content: <article>In addition to Epic Games announced a preview of their new Epic Games Launcher, including Linux support, they also announced plans to improve their Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) software on Linux. Along with this improved EAC they are also working on official Linux support for the popular Fortnite game...</article>
